summary: HAVEN is a health monitoring system for astronauts on long-duration missions, built for the challenge "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions." Far from Earth, communication delays and blackouts mean the crew must spot health changes themselves. HAVEN combines three parts: an iPhone app, an Apple Watch app and a web console for the ground team. The astronaut records 34 health indicators in five body zones (vital signs, sleep and mind, physical performance, metabolism and nutrition, environment) by hand, with on-screen cognitive tests or from the watch. A shared rules engine assesses each reading on the device itself and shows green, amber, red or pending, with the reason and the next action. An SOS on the watch starts an on-board emergency protocol that guides the crew even with no link to Earth. Everything is stored offline and sent to the ground console when the link returns, where the team reviews crew status, trends, KPIs and individual plans, helped by the ORION AI assistant. HAVEN matters because it helps astronauts evaluate and act on their health on their own, which is the core of the challenge. It is a decision-support prototype, not a medical device.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

HAVEN helps astronauts collect health indicators, understand their status and act on it, even when the link with Earth is delayed or down. It has three connected parts:

- Astronaut app (iPhone): records 34 indicators in five body zones (vital signs, sleep and mind, physical performance, metabolism and nutrition, environment). Readings come from manual entry, on-screen cognitive tests (reflexes, memory, attention) and the Apple Watch. It also includes a daily routine, individual medication and exercise plans, and modules for EVA readiness, motion sickness, reentry, workload and sample collection.

- Apple Watch: live heart rate and an SOS button (hold 3 seconds) that alerts the crew and Earth and opens the emergency protocol on the iPhone.

- Ground View (web console): mission control sees crew status, alerts, trends, KPIs and the packets each astronaut sends, assigns plans, and can ask ORION, an AI assistant that operates the console's features.

HOW IT WORKS

A shared rules engine runs on the device. It checks each reading against versioned thresholds, the astronaut's own baseline, the reading's age and the mission context, and returns green, amber, red or pending with the reason and the next action. Missing or old data is shown as pending, never as normal. Data is stored locally (SQLite) and sent to Earth as packets; with no link, packets wait in a queue and are sent when the link returns. Thresholds and plans are configuration, so the ground team can update them without reinstalling the app.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

On missions to the Moon or Mars, an answer from Earth can take many minutes. HAVEN gives the crew clear, explainable guidance on board, and gives the ground team one view of the whole crew once data arrives. Beyond spaceflight, the same approach fits analog habitats, Antarctic bases, submarines and remote expeditions.

TOOLS AND LANGUAGES

TypeScript monorepo (pnpm, Turborepo). Mobile: Expo SDK 58 / React Native, Expo Router, SQLite. Watch: Swift and SwiftUI. Web: Next.js 16, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, MongoDB Atlas, Vercel. AI assistant: AI SDK with OpenAI. Quality: Vitest (553 automated tests), Biome, GitHub Actions CI.

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

We designed for the worst case: no connection. Every assessment works offline, is explainable and is reproducible. We also considered accessibility, two languages (English and Spanish), and clear limits: HAVEN is a decision-support prototype, not a medical device, has no clinical validation and is not affiliated with NASA.

LINKS

Live Ground View: https://haven-eta-gray.vercel.app

Source code: https://github.com/Steven-Mendez/haven

Technical documentation and videos: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1gb3m8p6u3RM8QltIH59D_vnUakD15UGx

FULL REFERENCE LIST

The link lists above show our main sources. The complete list of NASA, space agency, medical and research references is in the Technical Documentation, section 8 (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1gb3m8p6u3RM8QltIH59D_vnUakD15UGx), and each indicator cites its sources in the code (https://github.com/Steven-Mendez/haven/tree/main/packages/core/config).

Open-source tools: Expo / React Native, Next.js, MongoDB Atlas, shadcn/ui, Tailwind, Turborepo, Vitest, Biome; hosted on Vercel.
